title: 虞美人·春花秋月
pinyin: Yú Měi Rén · Chūn Huā Qiū Yuè
englishTitle: Yu Meiren: Spring Flowers and Autumn Moon
author: Li Yu

translation: when will the spring flowers and autumn moon ever end
how much of the past do i still remember
the east wind visited my little tower again last night
i cannot bear to look back at my lost kingdom under the bright moon
the carved railings and jade steps should still be there
only the rosy faces have changed
i ask you, how much sorrow can a person hold
just like a river of spring water flowing east

appreciation: Li Yu, the captured last ruler of the Southern Tang, asks why the beautiful cycle of spring flowers and autumn moon refuses to end when his kingdom has. The carved palace should still stand, but the faces he knew are gone, and his sorrow pours out like a river of spring water. The poem matters because it turns one man's political ruin into a universal image of irreversible loss.
